summary: Peter Moran is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Tufts University and the University of Washington, where he completed his PhD under supervisor Charles F. Keyes.

Peter N. Gregory is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Smith College, and the Kuroda Institute.
Peter Peterson was an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai from circa 1873 to 1899.
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his MA at the University of Washington under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh. He served as an editor at the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies and was a professor at the University of Bonn from 2002 to 2018.

Peter Skilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. His posts include maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from 2002 to 2017.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who served as Associate Professor of Classical Art and Archaeology at the University of Oxford around 2011 and held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre in 2011.

Peter Zieme is a specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held posts at the German Academy of Sciences, the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Humboldt University, and the Free University of Berlin.

Peter van der Veer is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and sinology who studied at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University. He held posts at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, the University of Amsterdam, and the Max Planck Institute.

Peter von Bohlen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Georg Wilhelm Freytag. He was an associate professor at the University of Königsberg (1826–1828).

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dorpat, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Giessen, learning under Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth. He held a post at the University of Giessen from 1886 to 1896.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert. She held posts at the University of Göttingen (1980–1992) and the Academy of Sciences and Literature Mainz (circa 1993).

Petra Maurer is a scholar in Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dunchu Sonam Dorje and Dieter Schuh. She held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard University, SOAS, and Georgetown. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago and Harvard University, where he directed the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies from 1980 to 1986.

Philip A. Mellor is a religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester. He served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds.

Philip B. Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya. He served at Columbia University from circa 1968 to 1996 and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.
Philip Deslippe is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he also served as a teaching associate.

Philip J. Ivanhoe is a scholar of philosophy and sinology who earned his PhD at Stanford University. He held professorial posts at Stanford University, the University of Michigan, City University of Hong Kong, and Georgetown University.
